title: dfilter: Support directional double quotation marks
description:
Support the left double quotation mark (U+201C) in UTF-8 encoding
as beginning a double quoted string literal, and the right double
quotation mark (U+201D) as ending one. This mostly occurs when
filter examples are cut and paste from web pages or word processing
documents that "helpfully" substitute curly quotes for straight ones.

The right double quotation mark (but not the left) must now be
backslash escaped (or written in hex, octal, or the \u or \U
format). (An alternative to this would involve allowing string
literals to be surrounded by either a pair of straight double
quotes or a matching left and right directional double quotes, but
not a mix of straight and curly double quotes.)

notes.body: Should we switch to using hex for these? It seems to be more common.

Probably. The ease of reading it because most charts list hex probably overcomes the danger of accidentally making the escape sequence too long. I don't think we have any cases where we have to do some kind of horrible looking quoting to make a hex escape end because the next character would also be a valid hex digit.

commits_data.message:
dfilter: Support directional double quotation marks

Support the left double quotation mark (U+201C) in UTF-8 encoding
as beginning a double quoted string literal, and the right double
quotation mark (U+201D) as ending one. This mostly occurs when
filter examples are cut and paste from web pages or word processing
documents that "helpfully" substitute curly quotes for straight ones.

String literals can be surrounded by either a pair of straight double
quotes or a matching left and right directional double quotes, but
not a mix of straight and curly double quotes.

While doing this, convert the patterns in the flex for dfilter from
octal to hex, which is likely a little easier for people to read
these days, and it's what people are more likely to see if they look
up UTF-8 characters.
